svg.title: Reading the NaOH enthalpy–concentration chart (Foust Fig. 19.13)
svg.text: Reading the NaOH enthalpy–concentration chart (Foust Fig. 19.13)
NaOH–H₂O enthalpy–concentration chart (after McCabe), redrawn; isotherms every 20 °F; right: zooms
Feed: 10 % NaOH at 100 °F. Mark 10 % on the bottom axis and go up to the 100 °F isotherm.
From that point go across to the enthalpy axis. 3 → 4 h_F ≈ 60 Btu/lb.
Thick liquor: 50 % NaOH at its boiling point 233 °F (Dühring chart): mark 50 %, go up to the 233 °F
isotherm, interpolated between the 220 and 240 °F lines (dashed). 6 → 8 h_L ≈ 245 Btu/lb.
Hollow circle: this redraw’s value (≈ 248 Btu/lb at 50 %, 233 °F) where it differs from the solution’s reading.
Redrawn from the printed chart (digitized); in the exam read the printed chart — values may differ slightly.
